questions.q: A customer asks for a product that is out of stock. The best response is to:
o: say 'we don't have it' and walk away
tell the customer to shop elsewhere
offer to order it, suggest an alternative, or check another location
questions.x: Offering solutions keeps the sale and the relationship.

questions.q: Which action helps build rapport with a customer?
o: Checking your phone during the conversation
Using the customer's name and listening attentively
questions.x: Personal attention signals respect.

questions.q: Mirroring a customer's pace and tone (within professional limits) can help:
questions.x: Matching style helps customers feel understood.

questions.q: Patience is important in customer service because:
o: some customers need extra time to explain issues or make decisions
questions.x: Patience reduces frustration on both sides.

questions.q: A special request from a customer that is reasonable and within company policy should be:
questions.x: Flexibility within policy delights customers.

questions.q: Which nonverbal behavior shows a customer you are paying attention?
o: Maintaining appropriate eye contact and nodding
questions.x: Body language communicates interest.

questions.q: Responding to a customer inquiry you cannot answer, the best action is to:
o: tell the customer you will find out and follow up promptly
tell the customer it is not your job
questions.x: Honesty and follow-through build trust.

questions.q: A customer service mindset means:
o: putting the customer's needs first and taking ownership of solving problems
questions.x: Service-minded employees anticipate needs and follow through.

questions.q: The customer service mindset includes taking ownership, which means:
o: waiting for a manager to notice
accepting responsibility for resolving the customer's issue
passing the customer to another employee
questions.x: Ownership prevents customers from being bounced around.

questions.q: Anticipating unspoken customer needs means:
o: recognizing and meeting needs before the customer asks
questions.x: Example: offering an umbrella bag on a rainy day.

questions.q: Customer-focused businesses measure satisfaction using:
o: surveys, reviews, and Net Promoter Score
questions.x: Measurement identifies areas to improve.

questions.q: Customer relations refers to:
o: the way a business interacts with and builds goodwill among its customers
the company's tax relationship with the government
questions.x: Positive customer relations build loyalty and repeat business.

questions.q: Accommodating customers with disabilities is also required in many businesses by the:
questions.x: The ADA requires accessible public accommodations.

questions.q: Self-service options, such as online FAQs, benefit customers by:
o: providing quick answers at any time
questions.x: Customers often prefer quick self-service for simple issues.

questions.q: A customer emails a question. Good practice is to respond:
questions.x: Timely written responses show reliability.

questions.q: Internal customers are:
o: coworkers and departments within the organization who rely on your work
questions.x: Serving internal customers well supports external service.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between employee attitude and customer service?
o: Attitude has no effect on service
Positive employee attitudes lead to better customer experiences
questions.x: Employees' attitudes are visible to customers.

questions.q: Before putting a caller on hold, you should:
o: ask permission and wait for a response
transfer them to a random extension
questions.x: Courtesy maintains respect for the caller's time.

questions.q: When explaining a business policy that a customer dislikes, an employee should:
o: explain the reason for the policy politely and offer available alternatives
say 'that's just the rule' and walk away
change the policy on the spot without authority
questions.x: Interpreting policies with empathy keeps goodwill.

questions.q: Adapting communication to cultural differences includes:
o: being aware that gestures, eye contact, and personal space vary across cultures
questions.x: Cultural awareness prevents misunderstandings.

questions.q: Which approach is best when serving a customer who speaks limited English?
o: Speak clearly and simply, use visuals, and be patient
questions.x: Patience and clarity bridge language gaps.

questions.q: A customer in a wheelchair needs an item from a high shelf. The best response is to:
o: tell them to ask someone else
offer assistance and retrieve the item
questions.x: Accommodating special needs is part of excellent service.

questions.q: Customer loyalty is best described as:
o: a customer's commitment to repeatedly buy from a business
questions.x: Loyal customers are less price-sensitive and refer others.

questions.q: External customers are:
o: people outside the organization who buy its goods or services
questions.x: External customers generate revenue.

questions.q: Which question is an open-ended question that encourages a customer to explain their needs?
o: 'What will you be using the laptop for?'
questions.x: Open-ended questions invite detailed answers.

questions.q: Why is it more cost-effective to keep existing customers than to attract new ones?
o: Acquiring new customers typically costs more than retaining current ones
questions.x: Loyal customers also refer others.

questions.q: Personalized service means:
o: tailoring service to the individual customer's preferences
questions.x: Personalization makes customers feel valued.

questions.q: A customer service representative who follows up a week after a purchase to make sure the customer is satisfied is:
o: building and maintaining the customer relationship
violating privacy laws in all cases
questions.x: Follow-up shows care and identifies issues.

questions.q: Customer expectations are influenced by:
o: past experiences, advertising, word of mouth, and price
questions.x: Businesses must understand and manage expectations.

questions.q: Service recovery refers to:
o: actions taken to fix a service failure and restore customer satisfaction
questions.x: Good recovery can increase loyalty.

questions.q: Rapport with a customer is:
o: a relationship of trust and mutual understanding
questions.x: Rapport makes customers comfortable and open.

questions.q: Word of mouth is important in customer service because:
o: satisfied and dissatisfied customers share their experiences with others
it is a form of paid advertising
questions.x: Online reviews amplify word of mouth.

questions.q: Which telephone practice reflects good customer service?
o: Answering promptly with a greeting, your name, and the company name
Putting callers on hold without asking
questions.x: Professional phone etiquette creates a positive first impression.

questions.q: Net Promoter Score (NPS) is based on how likely customers are to:
questions.x: NPS asks a 0–10 likelihood-to-recommend question.

questions.q: An example of going above and beyond for a customer is:
o: telling them where the exit is
helping a customer carry heavy purchases to their car
questions.x: Small extra efforts create memorable service.

questions.q: Which is an example of reinforcing service orientation through communication?
o: 'I'd be happy to help you with that.'
questions.x: Positive language shows willingness to serve.

questions.q: Self-awareness in emotional intelligence means:
o: being aware of the store layout
recognizing your own emotions and how they affect your behavior
questions.x: Self-aware employees manage reactions better.

questions.q: Trust in a customer relationship is built by:
questions.x: Reliability and honesty create trust.

questions.q: Empathy in customer service means:
o: understanding and sharing the customer's feelings
agreeing with everything the customer says
questions.x: Empathy shows customers they are heard.

questions.q: An employee who feels angry after a difficult customer interaction should:
o: take it out on the next customer
post about it on social media
take a moment to calm down before serving the next customer
questions.x: Managing emotions protects future interactions.

questions.q: Self-regulation, a component of emotional intelligence, means:
o: controlling your emotional reactions, such as staying calm with an angry customer
questions.x: Self-regulation keeps interactions professional.

questions.q: Which behavior damages trust with a customer?
o: Making a promise and failing to keep it
questions.x: Broken promises erode credibility.

questions.q: Which statement expresses empathy to an upset customer?
o: 'I understand how frustrating that must be.'
questions.x: Acknowledging feelings defuses tension.

questions.q: Using a calm, steady voice with an upset customer helps to:
questions.x: Calmness is contagious.

questions.q: Paraphrasing what a customer says helps to:
o: confirm understanding and show you are listening
questions.x: 'So the order arrived damaged and you'd like a replacement?'

questions.q: Integrity in customer service means:
o: bending the truth to avoid conflict
being honest and acting ethically even when no one is watching
questions.x: Integrity builds lasting trust.

questions.q: Active listening involves:
o: planning your reply while the customer talks
giving full attention, asking clarifying questions, and summarizing what you heard
questions.x: Active listening ensures understanding.

questions.q: A customer's tone of voice, facial expressions, and posture are examples of:
questions.x: Reading nonverbal cues reveals unspoken feelings.

questions.q: Social awareness in emotional intelligence includes:
o: reading others' emotions through tone, words, and body language
questions.x: Social awareness helps adapt service.

questions.q: Emotional intelligence is the ability to:
o: recognize, understand, and manage your own emotions and the emotions of others
questions.x: EI includes self-awareness, self-regulation, empathy, and social skills.

questions.q: A customer shares a personal problem while shopping. An emotionally intelligent employee would:
o: listen respectfully and respond with appropriate empathy
tell the customer it is unprofessional
questions.x: Showing care strengthens relationships.

questions.q: Open, honest communication with customers includes:
o: admitting mistakes and explaining what will be done to fix them
questions.x: Transparency builds credibility.

questions.q: Respecting customers' time can be shown by:
o: sending them to the wrong department
serving them efficiently and acknowledging waits
questions.x: Acknowledgment ('I'll be right with you') matters.

questions.q: Treating customers with dignity and respect means:
o: being courteous to all customers regardless of their background or appearance
questions.x: Respect for all is a core service value.

questions.q: A difficult customer insists on a refund that policy does not allow. The best approach is to:
o: explain the policy, offer alternatives, and involve a supervisor if needed
questions.x: Offering options shows a desire to help.

questions.q: Apologizing to a customer who experienced a problem:
o: shows you care about their experience, even if you did not cause it
admits legal guilt in every case
questions.x: A sincere apology defuses anger.

questions.q: Escalating a complaint to a supervisor is appropriate when:
o: you want to avoid any work
the solution requires authority beyond yours
questions.x: Escalation should be smooth and explained.

questions.q: When a customer is angry and shouting, an employee should:
o: stay calm, listen, and avoid taking it personally
questions.x: Remaining calm de-escalates conflict.

questions.q: The LAST method for handling complaints stands for:
questions.x: LAST is a common service recovery model.

questions.q: A win-win resolution to a customer conflict is one in which:
o: both the customer and the business are satisfied with the outcome
questions.x: Collaborative problem solving seeks mutual benefit.

questions.q: The first step in handling a customer complaint is to:
o: explain why the customer is wrong
listen to the customer without interrupting
questions.x: Listening shows respect and reveals the real issue.

questions.q: Thanking a customer for a complaint is valuable because:
o: customers enjoy being thanked for anything
complaints give the business a chance to fix problems and improve
questions.x: Most unhappy customers leave without complaining.

questions.q: Documenting customer complaints helps a business:
o: identify recurring problems and improve service
questions.x: Patterns reveal systemic issues.

questions.q: An irate customer uses abusive language toward an employee. The employee should:
o: calmly set boundaries and follow company policy, involving a manager if needed
questions.x: Employees deserve respect; policies guide escalation.

questions.q: After resolving a complaint, the employee should:
o: tell coworkers the customer was difficult
follow up to ensure the customer is satisfied
questions.x: Follow-up confirms the fix worked.

questions.q: Which strategy helps resolve a service problem effectively?
o: Ask the customer to solve it
Identify the root cause and offer a solution the customer agrees to
Offer nothing until the customer leaves
questions.x: Solutions should address the cause.

questions.q: A company's service standards are:
o: specific guidelines for how employees should serve customers
questions.x: Example: answering calls within three rings.

questions.q: Empowering employees to solve customer problems without always asking a manager:
o: speeds up service recovery and improves satisfaction
questions.x: Empowered employees act quickly.

questions.q: Brand image is:
o: the perception customers have of a company
questions.x: Employee performance shapes brand image.

questions.q: A brand promise is:
o: what a company commits to delivering to customers every time
questions.x: Example: a delivery company promising on-time delivery.

questions.q: A 'moment of truth' in customer service is:
o: the moment a product is manufactured
the end of a fiscal year
any point of contact where a customer forms an impression of the business
questions.x: Each touchpoint shapes perception.

questions.q: Consistency in service means customers receive:
o: different service depending on the employee's mood
the same high level of service every time and at every location
questions.x: Consistency builds trust in the brand.

questions.q: Under-promising and over-delivering means:
o: promising more than you can deliver
setting realistic expectations and then exceeding them
questions.x: It manages expectations to create delight.

questions.q: Which is a negative moment of truth?
o: A customer waits 20 minutes on hold without updates
An employee greets a customer warmly
questions.x: Negative moments damage perception.

questions.q: Exceeding customer expectations often leads to:
questions.x: Delighted customers return and refer others.

questions.q: The customer experience includes:
o: every interaction the customer has with the company, from discovery to after-sale support
questions.x: CX spans the whole customer journey.

questions.q: A customer touchpoint is:
o: any interaction between a customer and the business, such as a website, phone call, or store visit
questions.x: Managing all touchpoints creates a cohesive experience.

questions.q: A store promises 'no-hassle returns.' An employee who argues with customers about returns is:
questions.x: Behavior must match the promise.

questions.q: A hotel that greets guests by name at check-in is delivering:
questions.x: Personal recognition creates a memorable impression.

questions.q: Which factor contributes most to a positive customer experience?
questions.x: People and processes shape experience.

questions.q: Professional appearance and a clean workspace support the brand because they:
questions.x: Physical evidence signals quality.

questions.q: Customer journey mapping helps businesses:
o: visualize each step customers take and improve pain points
questions.x: Maps reveal where experiences break down.

questions.q: Employees reinforce a company's brand image by:
o: delivering service consistent with the brand promise
questions.x: Every interaction reflects the brand.

questions.q: Meeting customer expectations is important because:
o: unmet expectations lead to dissatisfaction even if the service was adequate
questions.x: Satisfaction depends on expectations versus experience.

questions.q: Customer lifetime value (CLV) estimates:
o: the total revenue a business can expect from a customer over the entire relationship
questions.x: CLV justifies investing in retention.

questions.q: A CRM system typically stores:
o: customer contact information, purchase history, and service interactions
questions.x: Unified records help personalize service.

questions.q: Which is an example of an omnichannel customer service approach?
o: A customer starts a chat online and continues by phone without repeating information
Service is available only in person
questions.x: Integrated channels provide seamless service.

questions.q: Using CRM data to send a birthday discount to a customer is an example of:
questions.x: CRM enables targeted communication.

questions.q: Loyalty programs tracked through CRM reward customers for:
questions.x: Points and perks encourage repeat business.

questions.q: Chatbots in customer service are an example of:
o: technology used to provide quick automated responses
questions.x: Bots handle simple questions; humans handle complex ones.

questions.q: Customer relationship management (CRM) is:
o: a strategy and technology for managing interactions with current and potential customers
a type of accounting software for taxes
questions.x: CRM centralizes customer data to improve relationships.

questions.q: Logging every customer call in the CRM system helps because:
o: other employees can see what has already been discussed
questions.x: Shared records improve continuity.

questions.q: Customer segmentation within a CRM system allows a business to:
o: group customers by characteristics to tailor service and offers
questions.x: Segments support targeted strategies.

questions.q: An ethical concern in customer relationship management is:
o: protecting customers' personal data and privacy
questions.x: Businesses must secure data and use it responsibly.

questions.q: Customer data should be used:
o: only for purposes customers have agreed to and in compliance with privacy laws
questions.x: Transparency and consent are ethical requirements.

questions.q: A benefit of CRM technology for customer service representatives is that it:
o: gives them a customer's full history so they can resolve issues faster
questions.x: Context means customers do not have to repeat themselves.

questions.q: Cross-selling differs from upselling because cross-selling:
o: recommends complementary products, while upselling recommends a higher-end version
questions.x: Both increase sale value when done to help the customer.

questions.q: A prospect is:
questions.x: Prospecting identifies potential customers.

questions.q: Demonstrating a product during a sale is effective because it:
o: lets the customer see or experience the benefits
questions.x: Involving the senses increases understanding.

questions.q: A buying signal is:
o: a verbal or nonverbal clue that a customer is ready to buy
questions.x: Examples: asking about delivery or nodding in agreement.

questions.q: The first step in the selling process is often to:
o: approach the customer and establish a relationship
questions.x: A positive approach opens the conversation.

questions.q: A customer says, 'I need to think about it.' A helpful response is:
o: 'Of course. Is there anything I can clarify for you?'
questions.x: Uncover the real concern respectfully.

questions.q: Following up after a sale helps to:
o: pressure the customer to return items
ensure satisfaction and build repeat business
questions.x: Follow-up strengthens relationships.

questions.q: Closing the sale means:
o: asking the customer to make the purchase decision
questions.x: Closing is a natural step when the customer shows buying signals.

questions.q: The direct close involves:
questions.x: 'May I ring that up for you?'

questions.q: Suggestion selling is:
o: pressuring a customer to buy more than they need
recommending additional related items after the customer decides to buy
questions.x: Example: suggesting a case with a phone.

questions.q: A benefit of a product is:
o: the advantage the customer gains from a feature
questions.x: Example: 12-hour battery → 'lasts your whole school day.'

questions.q: Recommending a specific product should be based on:
o: the product with the highest commission
questions.x: Need-based recommendations build trust.

questions.q: The superior-point method of handling objections:
o: acknowledges the objection and presents features that outweigh it
questions.x: It admits a weakness but highlights stronger benefits.

questions.q: A feature of a product is:
o: a physical or functional characteristic, such as a 12-hour battery
how the product helps the customer
questions.x: Benefits explain why the feature matters.

questions.q: Ethical selling requires a salesperson to:
o: represent products honestly and recommend what truly meets the customer's needs
questions.x: Honesty sustains long-term relationships.

questions.q: Which closing technique assumes the customer has already decided to buy?
questions.x: 'Would you like it delivered Tuesday?'

questions.q: Determining customer needs is best accomplished by:
questions.x: Needs determination guides product recommendations.

questions.q: Establishing a relationship with a customer at the start of the sale is important because:
o: customers buy more readily from people they trust
questions.x: Trust precedes the sale.

questions.q: Consultative selling focuses on:
o: understanding the customer's problems and recommending solutions
pushing as many products as possible
questions.x: The salesperson acts as an advisor.

questions.q: An objection in selling is:
o: a concern or reason a customer gives for not buying
questions.x: Objections signal interest and need for information.

questions.q: The 'trial close' helps a salesperson:
o: test the customer's readiness to buy
questions.x: 'How does this color look with your setup?'

questions.q: After a customer agrees to buy, the salesperson should:
o: reassure the customer about the decision and complete the transaction smoothly
immediately try to sell an unrelated item aggressively
questions.x: Reassurance reduces buyer's remorse.

questions.q: When a customer asks detailed technical questions, the salesperson should:
o: answer accurately or find someone who can
questions.x: Accurate product knowledge builds credibility.

questions.q: Turning an objection into a reason to buy is called the:
questions.x: Example: 'It's heavy' → 'Its solid build makes it durable.'
